subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit per-agent delegate-only/self-deny tool policy, and which public config shape should own it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the change adds public config surface and changes how a security-sensitive deny boundary flows from requester agents to spawned subagents.

options.title: Approve delegate-only config
options.body: Add an optional per-agent policy that hides listed tools from the requester model while preserving absolute deny-wins behavior and controlled child inheritance.

options.title: Fold into child-side toolsAllow only
options.body: Treat per-spawn toolsAllow as the near-term child restriction surface and document that parent direct-use prevention still requires separate agent profiles or instructions.

options.title: Keep monotonic policy
options.body: Reject parent-deny delegation for now and document the security rationale plus the separate-agent workaround.

recommendation.title: Approve delegate-only config
recommendation.body: Add an optional per-agent policy that hides listed tools from the requester model while preserving absolute deny-wins behavior and controlled child inheritance.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining blocker is a public config and security-boundary choice, and Peter is the strongest available decision-routing signal from the prior review and live issue timeline.
